findings.description: _bdb_hd_exec_dest checks destination strings without normalizing path components. For example, /usr/local/bin/./helper misses both the bin-directory regex and a PATH entry of /usr/local/bin, so a tee heredoc writing executable content there is classified as nonexec.
findings.failure_mode: A command such as `tee /usr/local/bin/./helper <<'EOF'\nif true; then rm -rf /; fi\nEOF` has its body removed from the destructive-command scan: the segment words are if, then, and fi. Where the destination is writable, this allows overwriting a command on PATH with destructive shell content. Previously, tee heredocs received the full scan.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize literal destination paths before checking executable directories and PATH membership. If normalization cannot be established safely, retain the full body scan.

findings.description: The per-segment body scan (_bdb_hd_scan_body via _bdb_hd_segword) keeps a body line only when its first word, after wrapper stripping, is a fence verb. Shell keywords are not stripped: `if`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `do`, `while`, `until`, and `case` arm prefixes (`x)`) are returned as the command word, so `if :; then rm -rf /; fi` or `for f in x; do git push --force; done` is dropped entirely from a nonexec-classified body. A quoted-delimiter body is also exempt from the `$(` fallback, so `$(rm -rf /)` is dropped too. Nonexec classification is reachable for bodies that the same command executes: `cat <<'EOF' > t` followed on a later line by `bash t*`, `cat t | bash`, or `make` after writing `Makefile`, because _bdb_hd_same_line_exec only fires when the exact basename token appears outside a safe reader and never looks at where a safe reader's output is piped. Before this change the #1245 scrub only dropped a body for a standalone `cat <<'W' [> path]`, so a trailing executor kept the body in scope; the new default-on classifier is strictly looser here.
findings.failure_mode:
A Bash command such as `cat <<'EOF' > t
if :; then rm -rf /; fi
EOF
bash t*` (or `cat t | bash`, or `cat <<'EOF' > Makefile` + `make`) is reduced to `cat <<'EOF' > t
EOF
bash t*` before the fence rules run; the destructive command is neither matched nor asked about and executes.
findings.suggested_fix: In _bdb_hd_segword strip reserved words (if|then|else|elif|do|while|until|time|coproc|select, a leading `case`-arm `word)` prefix, and a leading `$(`) the same way wrappers are stripped so fence-verb segments are always kept regardless of classification. Separately harden _bdb_hd_same_line_exec: treat any token containing a glob or expansion that could resolve to the target as a hit, flag a safe-reader segment whose pipeline later reaches an interpreter (`cat t | bash`), and add implicit executors (make/npm/just/task after writing their manifests, .mcp.json, .github/workflows, .pre-commit-config.yaml) to _bdb_hd_exec_dest. Add corpus cases for each bypass shape in tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl.

findings.description: `git` and `gh` are on the safe-reader allowlist, so naming the heredoc's output file in a git/gh invocation on the same command never flips the class to interpreter. git executes configured helpers from its arguments: `git -c core.pager=./t log`, `git -c core.fsmonitor=./t status`, `git -c diff.external=./t diff`, `git config core.hooksPath dir`. gh runs `gh alias set --shell`. These are same-command executions of the heredoc body that the classifier currently accepts as non-executing.
findings.failure_mode: `cat <<'EOF' > t` + `git -c core.pager=./t log` keeps nonexec; with DISS-001 unfixed any keyword-prefixed destructive line in the body runs unscanned, and even after DISS-001 a non-verb payload (e.g. a credential exfil) bypasses the intended fence class.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop git and gh from _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader, or restrict them to a short allowlist of read-only subcommands (git status/log/diff/show without -c, gh pr/issue view/comment) and treat any `-c`/`config`/`alias` form as an executor.

findings.description: The new sanctioned_marker path grants an allow in every mode, including deny, whenever .run/implement-active.json exists with skill implement|bug and a started_at within two hours. The marker is written by run-checkpoint.sh mark, i.e. by the model through the Bash tool, which this gate does not see and which block-destructive-bash does not block. The same file's header states the tighten-only rule for model-authored claims (sprint-250 n17/n18: a claim may add an ask, never grant an allow); the marker is a model-authored claim that grants an allow and lifts the deny fence for two hours. The Write-tool trust-input ask does not cover a Bash write of the same file.
findings.failure_mode: Under implement_gate.mode: deny, a session denied on an App Zone write runs `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh mark implement S-1` (or `printf '{...}' > .run/implement-active.json`) via Bash and every subsequent App Zone write is allowed with decision sanctioned_marker for two hours, with no ask.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not let the marker sanction under deny (treat it as evidence that can raise an ask to allow only together with a fresh RUNNING cache), or bind the marker to something the model cannot forge from Bash (an HMAC over skill|sprint|started_at keyed from a lead-only secret, or a session id supplied by the harness) and verify it in check_implement_marker. Document whichever trust boundary is chosen in the header.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml sets guardrails.danger_level.enforce and guardrails.input.enabled to false under the default `standard` profile; danger-level-enforcer.sh and input_guardrails.md now resolve their enable flag through that profile instead of a built-in true.
findings.description: Before this change the danger-level enforcer was effectively always on (no config file → enabled; `// true` in yq also coerced an explicit false to true) and the pre-execution guardrails ran unless explicitly disabled. After it, both resolve through loa_knob with the `standard` profile defaulting to false, so any existing install whose .loa.config.yaml never set these keys silently loses both controls on upgrade. The profiles.yaml header calls this a migration item, but nothing in the diff warns the operator or offers a migration step, and the enforcer is also sourced unconditionally (`source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"` with no fallback), so a missing lib disables enforcement rather than failing closed.
findings.failure_mode: Repositories on the previous release that relied on default danger-level enforcement and input guardrails upgrade and continue to run with both off, without any surfaced notice; if profile-lib.sh is absent or errors, `loa_knob` is not defined, `enforce` is empty and enforcement is silently off.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a one-time WARN (or /loa status line) when a security knob resolves from the profile rather than an explicit key, and add a migration note to the release. In danger-level-enforcer.sh guard the source (`source … || { echo 'profile-lib missing' >&2; exit 2; }`) or fall back to enabled when the lib cannot be loaded.

findings.description: C-TEAM-001 through C-TEAM-005 (lead-only planning skills, serialized beads, lead-owned .run state, lead-coordinated git, teammate System Zone read-only) are deleted from constraints.json and the generated Agent Teams table is removed from CLAUDE.loa.md. Each cites a real incident (#337, bridgebuilder-horizon-pr341) and two claim mechanized enforcement (team-skill-guard.sh, a PreToolUse Write/Edit hook). The diff shows the prompt-layer removal but not the enforcement side; if the hooks were not also retained/updated, the only remaining guard for teammates is gone, and any script that validates or references these ids (validate-constraints.sh, lint-invariants.sh, the agent-teams reference) may now disagree with the data file.
findings.failure_mode: A teammate agent no longer sees the rules in CLAUDE.loa.md; if team-skill-guard.sh or the System Zone hook was removed or depends on these constraint ids, teammates can run planning skills, br commands, git commit/push, or edit .claude/ concurrently with the lead, reproducing incident #337.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm team-skill-guard.sh and the System Zone PreToolUse hook remain registered and do not look up C-TEAM ids; keep the rules in .claude/loa/reference/agent-teams-reference.md with an explicit pointer from the hooks; add a test that the hooks still deny a teammate write to .claude/ and a teammate `br` invocation.
